text.p: About 100 members of the Eurotunnel small shareholders' association staged a demonstration on Thursday outside the British Embassy in Paris to demand an extension of the tunnel concession for a total of 999 years.

Several shareholders led by association chairman Christian Cambier gathered outside the embassy's rear gates and presented a letter for the ambassador with their request for an extension of the operating licence in exchange for their approval of a pact to restructure 70 billion francs ($13.4 billion) of bank debt.

They chanted "The English with us for 999 years," and carried banners bearing slogans, "French and English together, let's save the tunnel" and "No to the insufficient concession of 60 years, Yes to the British model for a concession of 999 years".

"Today, officially, Mr Ambassador, we ask (you) immediately to intervene at the highest levels of the British state that the current concession be extended beyond 2052 and why not for 999 years," Cambier's open letter to the British ambassador said.
It said French President Jacques Chirac was favourable to the extension.

Cambier earlier told a shareholders' meeting at the nearby Auto Club de France that a granting of the concession extension was a condition for the association's approval for Eurotunnel's bank debt restructuring. "It's a condition sine qua non for our approval," he said.
Eurotunnel needs three-quarters majority shareholders' consent at an extraordinary general meeting for the debt deal.

The London and Continental Railways (LCR) consortium led by Richard Branson's Virgin Group has a 999-year concession on the high-speed link between London and Folkestone. The Channel Tunnel concession was extended in 1993 by 10 years to run 65 years and expires in 2052.
-- Pierre Tran, Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.215 French Francs)
